Whereas the Parliament of India has set out to provide a practical regime of right to 
information for citizens to secure access to information under the control of public authorities,

to the public, particularly disadvantaged communities and those engaged in the pursuit of 
education and knowledge, the attached public safety standard is made available to promote the 
timely dissemination of this information in an accurate manner to the public.

Indian Standard ( Reaffirmed 2002 ) 

SPECIFICATION FOR 

FORCEPS, GOUGE, ORTHOPAEDIC 

FERGUSSON'S PATTERN 



1. Scope — Dimensions and other requirements for gouge forceps Fergusson's pattern used in orthopaedic 
surgery. 

2. Material 

2.1 Arms — Stainless steel having the following composition: 

Percent 

Carbon 0-35 to 0*45 

Silicon l"0 Max 

Manganese 10 Max 

Chromium 12*5 to 14'5 

Nickel 1-0 Max 

Sulphur 0*03 Max 

Phosphorus 0*03 Max 

2.2 Springs — Stainless steel conforming to Designation 30 Crl3 of Schedule V of IS: 1570-1961 'Schedules 
for wrought steels for general engineering purposes'. 

1.3 Screws — Stainless steel conforming to Designation 22CH3 of Schedule V of IS: 1570-1961. 

3. Shape and Dimensions — As shown in Fig. I. 

4. Workmanship 

4.1 The forceps shall be free from rough edges, pits, burrs, cracks and blemishes of any kind. 

4.2 The cutting edges shall be sharp and uniform. 

4.3 When the jaws are closed, the cutting edges shall meet evenly. 

4.4 The joints shall have no undue play. 

4.5 The spring action shall be smooth. It shall be neither too hard nor too slack. 

5. Heat Treatment— The arms shall be hardened and tempered to 520 to 600 HV t the springs to 380 to 
420 HV and the screws to 290 to 320 HV. 

6. Finish — The forceps shall be finished smooth, passlvated and polished bright. 

7. Tests 

7.1 Performance Test — Cut a piece of rib of a fully grown goat or sheep five times with the instrument. 
Each time the instrument shall cut the rib neatly and evenly in one bit e without any undue resistance, 
and cutting edges shall not show any sign of damage. 

7.2 Load Closure Test — Apply a compressive force of 15 ± 2 N ( I -5 ± 0-2 kgf approximately ) at the ends 
of the handles. The cutting edges shall meet evenly. 

7.3 Corrosion Resistance Test — Scrub the instrument with soap and warm water, rinse in hot water and 
then dip in 95 percent ethyl alcohol. Dry the instrument, immerse in copper sulphate solution at room 
temperature for 6 minutes and wash with fresh water or wet cotton wool. The copper sulphate solution 
shall be made up as follows: 

Copper sulphate ( CuSOa.ShbO ) 40 g 

Sulphuric acid (H*SO*)(spgr 184) 10-0 g 

Distilled water (see IS: 1070-1960 Specification 90*0 ml 

for water,. distilled quality)

There shall be no red stains or spots on the instrument, but dulling of the polished surface may be 
permitted.

8. Marking — The forceps shall be marked with the following: 

a) Manufacturer's name, initials or recognized trade-mark; and 

b) Country of origin. 

8.1 JSf Certification Marking — Details available from the Indian Standards Institution. 

9. Packing — As agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier.
